nodes.label: Memory Networks
nodes.description: Introduced models that combine a learned inference component with a long-term read/write memory, the starting point of explicit memory for neural QA. https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.3916

nodes.label: Neural Turing Machines
nodes.description: Coupled a neural network to an external addressable memory trained end to end with differentiable read/write heads. https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.5401

nodes.label: End-To-End Memory Networks
nodes.description: A memory network trained end to end with soft attention over memory hops, removing the need for supervision of supporting facts. https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.08895

nodes.label: Key-Value Memory Networks
nodes.description: Split memory slots into keys and values so the model can read documents or knowledge bases directly for QA. https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03126

nodes.label: Attention Is All You Need
nodes.description: Introduced the Transformer, the architecture underlying all later retrieval-augmented and long-context language models. https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762

nodes.label: BERT
nodes.description: Bidirectional Transformer pre-training; its encoders became the backbone of dense retrievers and readers. https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805

nodes.label: Transformer-XL
nodes.description: Added segment-level recurrence and relative positions so a Transformer can attend to cached states beyond a fixed context. https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.02860

nodes.label: Compressive Transformers
nodes.description: Extended Transformer-XL's memory by compressing old activations instead of discarding them. https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.05507

nodes.label: DrQA: Reading Wikipedia to Answer Open-Domain Questions
nodes.description: Retriever-reader pipeline (TF-IDF retrieval plus neural reader) that framed open-domain QA over Wikipedia. https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.00051

nodes.label: ORQA: Latent Retrieval for Weakly Supervised Open Domain QA
nodes.description: Trained the retriever jointly with the reader from question-answer pairs only, using an inverse cloze pretraining task. https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.00300

nodes.label: kNN-LM: Generalization through Memorization
nodes.description: Interpolated a language model with nearest-neighbour lookups over a datastore of cached hidden states, with no retraining. https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00172

nodes.label: REALM
nodes.description: Pre-trained a masked language model together with a latent retriever over Wikipedia, backpropagating through retrieval. https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08909

nodes.label: DPR: Dense Passage Retrieval
nodes.description: Showed a dual-encoder dense retriever trained on a few thousand QA pairs beats BM25 for open-domain QA. https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04906

nodes.label: RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
nodes.description: Combined a parametric seq2seq generator with a non-parametric Wikipedia index (DPR) and named the RAG paradigm. https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401

nodes.label: Fusion-in-Decoder
nodes.description: Encoded each retrieved passage independently and fused them in the decoder, scaling generative QA to many passages. https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.01282

nodes.label: Distilling Knowledge from Reader to Retriever
nodes.description: Used reader attention scores as a training signal to learn a retriever without annotated passages. https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.04584

nodes.label: RocketQA
nodes.description: Improved dense passage retrieval training with cross-batch negatives, denoised hard negatives and data augmentation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.08191

nodes.label: ColBERT
nodes.description: Late interaction: per-token embeddings scored with MaxSim, giving cross-encoder-like quality at bi-encoder speed. https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.12832

nodes.label: ColBERTv2
nodes.description: Added residual compression and denoised supervision to ColBERT for a much smaller index and better quality. https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.01488

nodes.label: Contriever
nodes.description: Unsupervised dense retriever trained with contrastive learning that transfers well across domains. https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09118

nodes.label: SPLADE
nodes.description: Learned sparse retrieval using MLM-based term expansion and sparsity regularisation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.05720

nodes.label: HyDE: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
nodes.description: Has an LLM write a hypothetical answer document and retrieves with its embedding, enabling zero-shot dense retrieval. https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.10496

nodes.label: RETRO
nodes.description: Chunk-level retrieval from a 2-trillion-token database with cross-attention, matching much larger models with 25x fewer parameters. https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.04426

nodes.label: WebGPT
nodes.description: Fine-tuned GPT-3 to browse the web in a text browser and answer long-form questions with references, trained with human feedback. https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09332

nodes.label: GopherCite
nodes.description: Trained a language model to cite verbatim supporting quotes from retrieved documents, using RL from human preferences. https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11147

nodes.label: Atlas
nodes.description: Jointly pre-trained a retriever and a FiD reader, reaching strong few-shot results on knowledge-intensive tasks with a small model. https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03299

nodes.label: Memorizing Transformers
nodes.description: Added a kNN-retrieval attention layer over a non-differentiable memory of past key-value pairs. https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.08913

nodes.label: Internet-augmented LMs through few-shot prompting
nodes.description: Conditioned a language model on Google Search results via few-shot prompting to improve open-domain QA. https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.05115

nodes.label: Retrieval Augmentation Reduces Hallucination in Conversation
nodes.description: Showed retrieval-augmented dialogue models hallucinate less on knowledge-grounded conversation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07567

nodes.label: Internet-Augmented Dialogue Generation
nodes.description: Dialogue model that issues search-engine queries to ground its replies, with a Wizard of the Internet dataset. https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07566

nodes.label: SeeKeR
nodes.description: Modular search-then-knowledge-then-response generation for dialogue and prompt completion. https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.13224

nodes.label: LaMDA
nodes.description: Dialogue language models fine-tuned to consult external tools (retrieval, calculator, translator) for groundedness. https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.08239

nodes.label: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
nodes.description: Showed that few-shot reasoning traces in prompts elicit multi-step reasoning in large language models. https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11903

nodes.label: ReAct
nodes.description: Interleaved reasoning traces with tool actions (e.g. Wikipedia search), grounding LLM agents in retrieved evidence. https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629

nodes.label: Self-Ask: Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap
nodes.description: Prompts the model to ask and answer follow-up sub-questions, optionally with a search engine, for multi-hop questions. https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03350

nodes.label: Demonstrate-Search-Predict
nodes.description: Programs that pass natural-language texts between an LM and a retriever across multi-step pipelines (precursor of DSPy). https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.14024

nodes.label: IRCoT
nodes.description: Interleaves retrieval with chain-of-thought steps so each reasoning step guides the next retrieval. https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.10509

nodes.label: When Not to Trust Language Models (PopQA)
nodes.description: Introduced PopQA and showed retrieval helps long-tail facts while hurting popular ones, motivating adaptive retrieval. https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.10511

nodes.label: A Survey on Retrieval-Augmented Text Generation
nodes.description: First broad survey of retrieval-augmented text generation across dialogue, translation and other tasks. https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.01110

nodes.label: SQuAD
nodes.description: 100k+ crowd-written questions over Wikipedia paragraphs, the standard reading-comprehension benchmark. https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.05250

nodes.label: MS MARCO
nodes.description: Large machine-reading and passage-ranking dataset built from Bing queries; the main training set for neural retrievers. https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.09268

nodes.label: TriviaQA
nodes.description: Large distantly supervised reading-comprehension dataset of trivia questions with evidence documents. https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.03551

nodes.label: HotpotQA
nodes.description: Multi-hop QA dataset with sentence-level supporting facts, widely used for multi-step retrieval. https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.09600

nodes.label: Wizard of Wikipedia
nodes.description: Knowledge-grounded dialogue dataset where wizards ground replies in retrieved Wikipedia passages. https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.01241

nodes.label: Natural Questions
nodes.description: Real Google search queries paired with Wikipedia pages and annotated answers, the default open-domain QA benchmark. https://aclanthology.org/Q19-1026/

nodes.label: ELI5
nodes.description: Long-form question answering dataset from Reddit's Explain Like I'm Five. https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.09190

nodes.label: KILT
nodes.description: Unified benchmark of knowledge-intensive tasks all grounded in one Wikipedia snapshot. https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.02252

nodes.label: BEIR
nodes.description: Heterogeneous zero-shot benchmark of 18 retrieval datasets that exposed weak generalisation of dense retrievers. https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08663

nodes.label: MTEB
nodes.description: Massive benchmark of embedding tasks (including retrieval) across many datasets and languages. https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.07316

nodes.label: Toolformer
nodes.description: Self-supervised training of an LM to decide when to call tools such as search and a calculator. https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761

nodes.label: REPLUG
nodes.description: Treats the LM as a black box and prepends retrieved documents, with the retriever tuned to the LM's preferences. https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12652

nodes.label: In-Context Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
nodes.description: Prepends retrieved documents to the input of an unmodified LM, showing off-the-shelf retrieval improves language modelling. https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.00083

nodes.label: Fine-Tuning or Retrieval? Comparing Knowledge Injection in LLMs
nodes.description: Compares unsupervised fine-tuning with RAG for injecting new knowledge and finds RAG consistently better. https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.05934

nodes.label: FLARE: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
nodes.description: Retrieves anew when upcoming sentences contain low-confidence tokens, for long-form generation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.06983

nodes.label: Self-RAG
nodes.description: Trains an LM to emit reflection tokens that decide when to retrieve and critique retrieved passages and its own output. https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11511

nodes.label: Corrective RAG (CRAG)
nodes.description: Adds a retrieval evaluator that triggers web search and decompose-recompose filtering when retrieval is poor. https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.15884

nodes.label: Adaptive-RAG
nodes.description: Routes each question to no retrieval, single-step or multi-step RAG based on a query-complexity classifier. https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.14403

nodes.label: RA-DIT
nodes.description: Dual instruction tuning that separately updates the LM to use retrieved context and the retriever to supply what the LM prefers. https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01352

nodes.label: InstructRetro
nodes.description: Scaled RETRO-style retrieval-augmented pre-training to 48B and added instruction tuning. https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.07713

nodes.label: Retrieval meets Long Context LLMs
nodes.description: Compares retrieval and long-context windows and shows retrieval makes a short-context LLM competitive with a long-context one. https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.03025

nodes.label: Lost in the Middle
nodes.description: Showed LLM accuracy drops when relevant information sits in the middle of a long context. https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172

nodes.label: Dense X Retrieval (propositions)
nodes.description: Shows retrieving at proposition granularity beats passages or sentences. https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.06648

nodes.label: RAPTOR
nodes.description: Builds a tree of recursive cluster summaries and retrieves across levels for long documents. https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.18059

nodes.label: GraphRAG: From Local to Global
nodes.description: Builds an entity knowledge graph with community summaries to answer corpus-wide, query-focused summarisation questions. https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130

nodes.label: HippoRAG
nodes.description: Hippocampus-inspired long-term memory: knowledge graph plus Personalized PageRank for single-step multi-hop retrieval. https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14831

nodes.label: LightRAG
nodes.description: Graph-based RAG with dual-level (entity and theme) retrieval and incremental updates, cheaper than GraphRAG. https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05779

nodes.label: MemoRAG
nodes.description: Uses a light long-range LLM to form global memory and draft clues that guide retrieval. https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.05591

nodes.label: M3-Embedding
nodes.description: Single embedding model supporting dense, sparse and multi-vector retrieval in 100+ languages and long inputs. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03216

nodes.label: ColPali
nodes.description: Applies ColBERT-style late interaction to page screenshots with a vision-language model for visual document retrieval. https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01449

nodes.label: Searching for Best Practices in RAG
nodes.description: Empirically compares RAG pipeline components (retrieval, reranking, repacking, summarisation) to recommend a design. https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01219

nodes.label: Ragas
nodes.description: Reference-free metrics (faithfulness, answer and context relevance) for evaluating RAG pipelines. https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15217

nodes.label: ARES
nodes.description: Trains lightweight judges with synthetic data and prediction-powered inference to score RAG systems. https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09476

nodes.label: RGB: Benchmarking LLMs in RAG
nodes.description: Tests noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration and counterfactual robustness of RAG. https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.01431

nodes.label: CRUD-RAG
nodes.description: Chinese RAG benchmark covering create, read, update and delete scenarios. https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.17043

nodes.label: MultiHop-RAG
nodes.description: Benchmark of multi-hop queries over a news corpus for RAG systems. https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.15391

nodes.label: CRAG: Comprehensive RAG Benchmark
nodes.description: Dynamic factual-QA benchmark with mock web and knowledge-graph APIs across five domains. https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04744

nodes.label: FRAMES: Fact, Fetch, and Reason
nodes.description: Evaluates factuality, retrieval and multi-hop reasoning of RAG in a single end-to-end dataset. https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12941

nodes.label: BRIGHT
nodes.description: Retrieval benchmark requiring intensive reasoning to match queries to documents. https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.12883

nodes.label: RULER
nodes.description: Synthetic long-context benchmark beyond needle-in-a-haystack, measuring effective context size. https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06654

nodes.label: LongBench
nodes.description: Bilingual multi-task benchmark for long-context understanding. https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14508

nodes.label: BABILong
nodes.description: Reasoning-in-a-haystack benchmark that hides bAbI facts in very long text. https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10149

nodes.label: MEMORYLLM
nodes.description: Embeds a fixed-size memory pool in the LM's latent space that is updated with new knowledge. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04624

nodes.label: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
nodes.description: Neural long-term memory module updated at test time, combined with attention for contexts beyond 2M tokens. https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00663

nodes.label: Generative Agents
nodes.description: Agents with a memory stream, reflection and planning, retrieving by recency, importance and relevance. https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442

nodes.label: Reflexion
nodes.description: Agents store verbal self-reflections in an episodic memory buffer to improve later trials. https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366

nodes.label: Voyager
nodes.description: Minecraft agent with a growing skill library of retrievable code as long-term procedural memory. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291

nodes.label: MemoryBank
nodes.description: Long-term memory for LLM companions with Ebbinghaus-inspired forgetting and memory summarisation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10250

nodes.label: MemGPT
nodes.description: Treats the LLM context like an OS: pages data between main context and external storage through function calls. https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560

nodes.label: CoALA: Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents
nodes.description: Conceptual framework organising language agents around working, episodic, semantic and procedural memory. https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02427

nodes.label: ReadAgent
nodes.description: Paginates a long text, writes gist memories, and looks up original pages on demand. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09727

nodes.label: RAG for LLMs: A Survey
nodes.description: Organises RAG into naive, advanced and modular paradigms covering retrieval, generation and augmentation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.10997

nodes.label: Survey on the Memory Mechanism of LLM-based Agents
nodes.description: Reviews how memory is designed, evaluated and applied in LLM agents. https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.13501

nodes.label: LoCoMo
nodes.description: Very long (300-turn) multi-session conversations with QA, summarisation and event tasks for agent memory. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17753

nodes.label: LongMemEval
nodes.description: 500 questions testing information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, updates and abstention in chat assistants. https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813

nodes.label: A-MEM
nodes.description: Zettelkasten-style agentic memory where notes are linked and evolve as new memories arrive. https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12110

nodes.label: Zep
nodes.description: Temporal knowledge-graph memory (Graphiti) for agents that tracks how facts change over time. https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13956

nodes.label: Mem0
nodes.description: Production memory layer that extracts, consolidates and retrieves salient facts, with a graph variant. https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19413

nodes.label: Memory OS of AI Agent
nodes.description: Hierarchical short-, mid- and long-term memory with OS-style storage, updating and retrieval modules. https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06326

nodes.label: MIRIX
nodes.description: Multi-agent memory with six typed stores (core, episodic, semantic, procedural, resource, vault). https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.07957

nodes.label: Memory-R1
nodes.description: Reinforcement learning trains one agent to manage memory operations and another to answer from memory. https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.19828

nodes.label: Mem-alpha
nodes.description: RL-trained agent that learns how to construct and update memory from interaction streams. https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25911

nodes.label: MemAgent
nodes.description: RL-trained agent that reads long text in chunks and overwrites a fixed-size memory, extrapolating to millions of tokens. https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02259

nodes.label: MemoryAgentBench
nodes.description: Evaluates memory agents on accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding and conflict resolution. https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.05257

nodes.label: BrowseComp
nodes.description: Hard-to-find, easy-to-verify questions that test persistent web-browsing agents. https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.12516

nodes.label: Search-R1
nodes.description: Trains an LLM with reinforcement learning to interleave reasoning with search-engine calls. https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09516

nodes.label: R1-Searcher
nodes.description: Two-stage outcome-based RL that teaches LLMs to invoke search during reasoning. https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05592

nodes.label: Agentic RAG: A Survey
nodes.description: Taxonomy of agentic RAG architectures built on reflection, planning, tool use and multi-agent collaboration. https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09136

nodes.label: Memory in the Age of AI Agents
nodes.description: Survey of agent memory by forms, functions and dynamics, separating it from RAG and context engineering. https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.13564
